Wrapped statements must be separated from adjacent method statements by an empty line.

What The Standard says

“Abstraction” — Canonical Standard implementations use whitespace around wrapped multi-statement regions to keep the method's sequential flow readable. read it here.
“Testing” — The Standard's tests separate setup, execution and assertions into visible regions. Wrapped statements receive the same boundary so they do not blend into neighboring work. read it here.

Why it matters

Wrapped statements already demand extra attention, so surrounding whitespace should expose them as complete units. Consistent separation prevents dense formatting from hiding where one operation ends and another begins.

Bad code example

// Violates STXFORMAT008: Wrapped statements must be separated from adjacent method statements by an empty line.
Validate();
Student student = service.GetStudent(
    studentId: studentId);
Submit(student);

Good code example

// Follows STXFORMAT008
Validate();

Student student = service.GetStudent(
    studentId: studentId);

Submit(student);
